correctness.rationale: At any fixed lambda>0 each Haar detail is either active or inactive on an open soft-threshold chamber, and all 0/1 masks occur. Piecewise-affine segment integration reduces the sharp two-input path-variation Lipschitz norm to the maximum norm of the corresponding Haar subprojections. Constants are fixed and the path seminorm unit ball reduces exactly to one-jump vectors. For each cut only its dyadic ancestor wavelets contribute, and their left/right endpoint signs permit an exact nine-state recursion R_n^(p,q)(k) with p,q in {-1,0,1}; root center/left/right cases were checked. Disjoint dyadic support gradients at levels 0,3,6,... give the all-depth logarithmic lower bound and each scale contributes ≤2 for upper bound. Independently enumerated direct Haar projection masks and cut inputs for d=1..6: sharp values 1,3/2,2,21/8,3,117/32 matched recursive values to numerical precision; finite enumeration corroborates but does not establish all-depth recurrence and growth.
residual_risks: The theorem uses real orthonormal dyadic Haar on a nonperiodic path, common positive threshold, unthresholded constant and unrestricted real signal pairs. Claimed exact determination is a recurrence, not a closed formula for arbitrary depth.
